calculator.metaTitle: FRP profile calculator — beam analysis and steel replacement
calculator.metaDescription: FRP pultruded profile engineering calculator: beam deflection / bending stress analysis, steel-to-FRP equivalence, supports EN 13706, GB/T 31539, ASCE.
calculator.subtitle: Beam deflection & bending stress · Steel/aluminium → FRP equivalence
calculator.disclaimer: Reference: EN 13706-3, GB/T 31539-2015, ASTM D3917, ASCE pre-standard. Results are for preliminary sizing only — verify with detailed engineering calculations.
calculator.scaleNote: Scale factor ×{scale} — stiffness-matched (EI). Strength check may allow smaller sizes.
calculator.governingHintAl: When replacing aluminum with FRP, stiffness and strength criteria are often comparable — the FRP profile must satisfy BOTH, so the larger scale factor governs.
calculator.governingHintSteel: When replacing steel with FRP, stiffness almost always governs because FRP modulus is roughly 1/10 of steel.
calculator.equivDisclaimer: Based on geometrically similar scaling with both equal-stiffness (EI) and equal-strength (σW) suggestions per EN 13706-3, GB/T 31539-2015 and ASCE pre-standard. FRP design must satisfy both criteria — the larger scale factor governs. Verify with detailed engineering calculations.

uvalue.metaTitle: GFRP-PU Window U-Value Calculator — per JG/T 571-2019 App. C
uvalue.metaDescription: Whole-window U-value (Uw) and thermal grade for glass-fiber reinforced polyurethane (GFRP-PU) windows, based on JG/T 571-2019 Appendix C configuration table. Compared against Chinese and international energy codes.
uvalue.subtitle: Based on JG/T 571-2019 (GFRP-PU energy-saving windows) Appendix C whole-window heat-transfer table · Uw and thermal grade
uvalue.stdBadge: Per JG/T 571-2019 Appendix C, Table C.1 (frame-to-glass ratio 30:70)
uvalue.gasLocked: Gas fill fixed by this glass build
uvalue.customNote: Actual-size mode uses the JGJ/T 151 / EN ISO 10077-1 area-weighted method; the frame-to-glass ratio follows your dimensions, while Uf, Ug and the edge Ψ are taken from JG/T 571 Appendix C and Note 1. Result is an estimate — final rating requires hot-box testing (GB/T 8484).
uvalue.cmpTitle: vs Aluminium / PVC / Timber — whole-window comparison
uvalue.cmpSub: Whole-window U-value with only the frame material swapped, at the same glass build (30:70 frame-to-glass, casement). GFRP-PU reaches excellent insulation with no thermal break, thanks to low conductivity plus multi-chamber profiles.
uvalue.cmpHeadline: At the same glass build, whole-window U-value is {pct}% lower than aluminium with no thermal break
uvalue.cmpNote: Comparison-frame Uf values are typical industry references (not JG/T 571 data); whole-window Uw is estimated by swapping only the 30% frame contribution at the same glass and frame-to-glass ratio. Aluminium conducts heat ~440x more than GFRP-PU and must rely on a thermal break; PVC/timber conduct less but fall short of composites in stiffness, durability and dimensional stability.
uvalue.seriesTableTitle: JG/T 571 frame U-value Uf by series
uvalue.seriesTableSub: Frame U-value of each series in Appendix C Table C.1 (wider series = lower Uf = better insulation) and the best whole-window Uw each series can reach (argon-filled).
uvalue.note1: Note 1: Linear thermal transmittance at the frame-glass junction — ordinary glass 0.04 W/(m·K), Low-E glass 0.06 W/(m·K); with warm-edge spacers, double glazing 0.04 (table value -0.1), triple glazing 0.03 (table value -0.15).
uvalue.note2: Note 2: GFRP-PU material thermal conductivity is approximately 0.36 W/(m·K).
uvalue.note3: Note 3: Profile cavities must be filled with graphite EPS, PU or similar foam with conductivity ≤ 0.033 W/(m·K); otherwise the whole-window U-value increases by 0.15 W/(m²·K).
uvalue.note4: Note 4: For sliding doors/windows the profile width is taken as (frame + sash)/2, and the whole-window U-value increases by 0.3 W/(m²·K) over the table value.
uvalue.note5: Note 5: All Low-E glass shown is high-transmittance.
uvalue.citation: Source: JG/T 571-2019 'Glass-fiber reinforced polyurethane energy-saving doors and windows', Appendix C (informative), whole-window heat-transfer configuration Table C.1 (frame-to-glass ratio 30:70). Whole-window U-values are taken from this table with Note 3 / Note 4 corrections; thermal grading per GB/T 31433, test method per GB/T 8484-2020.
uvalue.stdTableSub: Maximum allowable whole-window U-value (Uw) under major Chinese and international building energy codes, for export and multi-market selection.
uvalue.stdDisclaimer: Method: Whole-window U-values are based on JG/T 571-2019 Appendix C (frame-to-glass ratio 30:70); the 'actual size' mode estimates Uw via EN ISO 10077-1 / JGJ/T 151 area weighting. Final rating must follow GB/T 8484-2020 hot-box testing; NFRC (US/CA) ratings require NFRC 100 simulation (THERM + WINDOW). Data is for reference; defer to current local standards.
uvalue.sizeError: Window too small for the chosen frame face width. Increase width or height.

uvalueIntl.metaTitle: Window U-value calculator — FRP frame thermal performance
uvalueIntl.metaDescription: Calculate whole-window U-value (Uw) per EN ISO 10077-1. Compare FRP, aluminium, PVC and timber frames. Check international energy codes.
uvalueIntl.subtitle: Whole-window U-value per EN ISO 10077-1 · Frame / glass / spacer comparison
uvalueIntl.vsAluText: Thermal performance is {pct}% better than aluminium without thermal break (U_w = {uw} W/m²K).
uvalueIntl.frameCmpSub: Frame U-values used in this calculator. FRP frames have inherently low conductivity — no thermal break required.
uvalueIntl.stdTableSub: Maximum allowable whole-window U-values in major building energy codes. Residential unless noted.
uvalueIntl.stdDisclaimer: Calculation note: This tool uses the simplified method of EN ISO 10077-1. NFRC (US/Canada) ratings require NFRC 100 simulation (THERM + WINDOW). Chinese GB compliance requires hot-box testing per GB/T 8484-2020. For reference only.

Fibers.s4Lead: These are industrially mainstream pairings for this fiber system; process parameters live under /tech and the formula library.

glass.lead: Glass fiber is the world's most-produced and most widely used reinforcement fiber. China carries more than 60% of global capacity. It is the cost-performance benchmark across pultrusion, hand lay-up, winding, SMC and RTM, and pairs with UPR / VER / epoxy / phenolic to cover applications from bathroom composites to wind blades.
glass.appBody1: Wind blade spar & shell · Pultruded profiles (window frames / gratings / cable trays) · Chemical storage tanks & piping · FRP marine hulls · Automotive parts · PCB electronics · Construction reinforcement.
glass.appBody2: Low cost (¥ 4-7 /kg) · Mature processes (pultrusion / RTM / SMC fully supported) · ECR offers good corrosion resistance · S-glass approaches aerospace strength. Complete domestic supply chain, short lead times.
glass.aiCtaTitle: Let AI pick the grade + process
glass.aiCtaBody: Describe your load case — stress, environment, process. AI recommends glass fiber grade, resin and process from 4,300+ materials and 100+ formulas, with citations.
glass.aiSuggestQuery: Glass fiber selection: product is [scenario], constraints [stress/environment] — recommend E-glass / ECR / S-glass? Which resin? Which process? Major suppliers?

carbon.lead: Carbon fiber sits at the top of the performance pyramid — specific strength and modulus far surpass glass fiber. T300 → T1000 covers everything from consumer (wind / automotive lightweighting / sports) to aerospace primary structure. Zhongfu Shenying / Guangwei / Hengshen have reached T800 aerospace-grade domestic production; Toray remains the high-end benchmark.
carbon.appBody1: Aerospace primary structure (wing / fuselage / doors) · Pultruded rods for wind blade spar caps · Automotive CFRP (B-pillar / battery shell / roof — HP-RTM) · High-pressure hydrogen tanks · Sports equipment · Satellite structure.
carbon.appBody2: 5–10× specific strength of steel · High specific modulus · Fatigue-tolerant · Corrosion-resistant. Downsides: expensive (¥ 120-500 /kg) · Complex processes (autoclave / HP-RTM / AFP) · Strict resin requirements (epoxy / BMI / PEEK). Best when performance-to-weight is the deciding factor.
carbon.aiCtaTitle: Let AI pick the grade + process
carbon.aiCtaBody: Describe the load case; AI compares T300 / T700 / T800 / M40J / M55J and recommends process + supplier.
carbon.aiSuggestQuery: Carbon fiber selection: [scenario] with [strength/modulus/cost/process] requirements — recommend T300 / T700 / T800 / T1000 / M40 / M55? Which resin? Which process? Chinese vs imported?

basalt.lead: Basalt fiber (BF) is a single-component natural mineral fiber drawn directly from basalt rock. It offers S-glass-like strength, higher temperature capability than glass fiber (700 °C), excellent alkali and corrosion resistance, and is fully green and recyclable. Rising in 'green alternative' and 'alkali-resistant reinforcement' applications.
basalt.appBody1: Alkali-resistant rebar for concrete (GFRP substitute) · Automotive chassis parts · Bridge retrofit · High-temperature pipes · Fire-retardant panels · Fire-blocking textiles · Battery insulation.
basalt.appBody2: 700 °C service — far above glass fiber · Better alkali resistance than E-glass — ideal for concrete reinforcement · Natural mineral origin · Cost ¥ 25-35 /kg (between glass and carbon) · Mature domestic supply chain.
basalt.aiCtaTitle: Let AI evaluate a basalt-fiber plan
basalt.aiCtaBody: AI compares glass / basalt / carbon for your load case and budget.
basalt.aiSuggestQuery: Is basalt fiber suitable for my [scenario]? Compared to ECR glass and carbon fiber? Which resin and process? Who are the main Chinese suppliers?

aramid.lead: Aramid, famously DuPont's Kevlar, is the benchmark fiber in ballistic / protective / reinforcement applications — high strength, very low density (1.44 g/cm³, 1/5 of steel), cut-resistant, self-extinguishing at 400 °C. Para-aramid (Kevlar) for structural reinforcement; meta-aramid (Nomex) for fire-retardant textiles. China's Taihe is already the world's #2 aramid supplier.
aramid.appBody1: Ballistic armor / helmets · Cut-resistant gloves · Optical cable reinforcement · Firefighter suits and fire-retardant materials · Automotive brake pads · Honeycomb cores · Aerospace rigid structure (hybrid laminates with carbon fiber).
aramid.appBody2: High energy absorption (~2× specific energy of carbon) · Cut / puncture resistant · LOI ≥ 28%, self-extinguishing · Lightweight. Downsides: high moisture uptake (interface treatment needed) · Low compressive strength · UV aging · ¥ 100-300 /kg.
aramid.aiCtaTitle: Let AI plan your aramid layup
aramid.aiCtaBody: Ballistic / protective / reinforcement — AI recommends Kevlar / Twaron / domestic para-aramid grades and layup strategy.
aramid.aiSuggestQuery: Aramid fiber selection: I'm building [ballistic / protective / structural reinforcement] needing [velocity / thickness / weight] — Kevlar 29 / 49 / 149 or domestic Taihe / Hongyi? Layup? Resin?

bio.lead: Bio-based fibers (flax / hemp / bamboo / ramie / jute) are the new frontier in automotive lightweighting and eco-friendly construction. EU recyclability regulations and automaker ESG targets have landed Bcomp's flax fiber in BMW / Porsche / Volvo interiors. Carbon footprint is just 1/5 of glass fiber.
bio.appBody1: Automotive interior (BMW M4 CSL seats / doors) · Sports equipment (skis / tennis rackets) · Bio-based construction · Packaging · Eco-friendly home goods · EV lightweight structural parts.
bio.appBody2: Carbon footprint 80% lower than glass · Biodegradable · Excellent damping (high-frequency vibration −20%) · Moderate cost ¥ 15-40 /kg. Downsides: hygroscopic (surface treatment required) · Temperature limit 200 °C · Lower mechanical strength than glass fiber · Batch-to-batch variation needs tight QC.

bio.aiSuggestQuery: Are bio-based fibers suitable for my [automotive / construction / home goods] scenario? Flax vs hemp vs ramie? Bio-epoxy or UPR? Chinese suppliers? ESG compliance?

Architecture.metaDescription: From AI Agent to structured data to engineering delivery, a detailed view of f1frp's three-layer technical architecture.
Architecture.h1: AI Agent × Structured Data × Engineering Delivery
Architecture.lead: The base of f1frp is not just a database website. It is a three-layer stacked system: the top AI Agent layer consumes the two below it, the middle data layer is a knowledge graph of six interlinked libraries, and the bottom engineering layer turns answers into artifacts engineers can ship with.
Architecture.s1Title: Each layer owns its role and feeds the others
Architecture.layer1Body: Dual-model routing: Gemini 2.5 Flash and Claude Haiku via OpenRouter. pgvector RAG retrieves embeddings across the six libraries, citation-first enforces source attribution. Question → semantic retrieval → sourced answer, never fabricated.
Architecture.layer2Body: Six interlinked tables: materials (4,341) · formulas (102) · standards (95) · papers (698+) · patents (1,473+) · supplier_listings (67). Every parameter traces to its source, every slug deep-linkable via hash anchor.
Architecture.layer2Stack: STACK · Neon Postgres · Drizzle ORM · pgvector · Zod schema
Architecture.layer3Body: RFQ form → Resend email to suppliers; download tier gating; PDF report generation; online calculators (pultrusion selection / U-value); zh/en language switch; Clerk auth + enterprise claim flow.
Architecture.layer3Stack: STACK · Next.js 16 App Router · next-intl · Clerk · Resend · Vercel
Architecture.s2Title: Four design choices that let the system self-run
Architecture.m1Body: Material pages show related formulas / recommended suppliers / downloads; paper pages show related papers; patent pages show related patents. Every page is an entry to the other five libraries.
Architecture.m2Body: Every number and statement in an AI answer carries a [#N] citation that clicks to the source paper/patent/material page. When no source supports a claim, the AI says so explicitly — no hallucination.
Architecture.m3Body: next-intl path prefix /zh/ + /en/, default zh as-needed. One schema, two language renders, SEO hreflang bidirectional, llms.txt for LLM crawlers.
Architecture.m4Body: Daily cron: CrossRef/OpenAlex/USPTO ingestion + RSS news → AI Chinese commentary → multi-engine push (Baidu/Bing/Sogou/360) → Telegram channel → weekly newsletter. Self-running, no manual toil.
Architecture.cta: Now that you know the architecture, see what advantages it produces:

Advantages.metaTitle: Advantages — why f1frp differs from traditional composites sites
Advantages.metaDescription: Six structural differences from traditional composites news/directory/e-commerce platforms.
Advantages.h1: Why we are different from traditional composites sites
Advantages.lead: Most traditional composites sites are stuck in Web 2.0: news + yellow pages + PDF downloads. f1frp's six structural differences are not single-feature wins — the entire operating model is different, which is what makes content and traffic compound.
Advantages.a1Body: Most other 'AI assistants' are ChatGPT-with-a-skin and hallucinate freely. f1frp's AI must source every statement from the six libraries; the [#N] markers are clickable and go to the source. No source → the AI says so.
Advantages.a2Body: CrossRef + OpenAlex + Google Patents + RSS, four pipelines in parallel. Papers went 101 → 698, patents 13 → 1,473 in a handful of bulk runs. Traditional sites depend on manual entry; here, the code produces content daily.
Advantages.a3Body: Not a Chinese site with English bolted on — one dataset, two renders. /zh/ + /en/ path prefix, hreflang bidirectional, llms.txt for LLMs. Covers Baidu / Sogou / Google / Bing / ChatGPT / Perplexity simultaneously.
Advantages.a4Body: Every paper ingested auto-triggers Chinese commentary + related material/standard/formula links + sitemap refresh + six-engine push + Telegram channel + weekly newsletter. Once a user lands, there is always more to read.
Advantages.a5Body: Materials / formulas / standards / papers / patents / suppliers are not isolated. Material pages recommend suppliers, formula pages link materials, paper pages show related patents. Any page is an entry to the other five.
Advantages.a6Body: Each material parameter carries a source type (manufacturer TDS / third-party test / AI inference), extensible to confidence labels. Papers link out to DOI, patents to publication number + Google Patents. Engineers know exactly where the data comes from.

Capabilities.metaDescription: Six core capabilities plus four typical workflow scenarios describing what engineers, buyers and suppliers get today.
Capabilities.h1: What you can take out of the site today
Capabilities.lead: Features are not better because there are more. We picked six capabilities to make usable, then layered four typical workflows — telling engineers, buyers and suppliers what problems they can each solve by walking in.
Capabilities.c1Body: Describe the load case (stress, chemistry, temperature, budget) to the AI; it recommends materials from the full material + formula + standard library, every recommendation with a source link.
Capabilities.c1Try: TRY · /ai?q=which resin resists HCl for storage tank
Capabilities.c2Body: 698+ papers and 1,473+ patents in one place, each carrying an AI Chinese commentary that translates English abstracts into engineer-readable digests — no need to wrestle CrossRef yourself.
Capabilities.c3Body: On any material detail page, the "Request Sample / Quote" button opens an RFQ form. AI matches top-3 suppliers, Resend emails them — all automatic.
Capabilities.c4Body: Pultruded profile selection (load → section recommendation), window U-value calculation. Run in the browser, no CAE license needed.
Capabilities.c5Body: 95 GB / ISO / ASTM / EN standards organized by process and product. Each with AI clause digest — no PDF wrestling.
Capabilities.c6Body: 67 verified composite firms. Companies can claim their own listings, complete profile for exposure.
Capabilities.sc1Title: Engineer: from load case to selection to RFQ
Capabilities.sc1Body: Describe load → AI recommends materials + suppliers → click detail → request sample → supplier gets email → sends sample. End-to-end on site, no context switch.
Capabilities.sc2Body: Filter supplier directory by region / type → inspect certifications / products → send RFQ → compare replies. Every decision data point carries a source.
Capabilities.sc3Title: Design firm / research institute: paper & patent verification
Capabilities.sc3Body: /pultrusion or /hp-rtm verticals give you all related papers + patents directly; each has Chinese commentary; every claim you use in your proposal is verifiable.
Capabilities.sc4Body: Claim your firm in /suppliers → complete products / certifications / contact → start receiving engineer-initiated RFQ emails.

Matrix.metaDescription: Following drug-discovery and chemistry-database playbooks, we organize composites along a fiber × resin × process three-dimensional matrix. Every cell links to a precise subset of the six knowledge libraries.
Matrix.lead: Organize composites along a fiber × resin × process three-dimensional grid. 5 fibers × 11 resins × 8 processes = 440 possible combinations; every cell is an engineering answer, linked to a precise subset of our six knowledge libraries (materials / formulas / standards / papers / patents / suppliers).
Matrix.s1Title: Organize composites like drug discovery and chemistry databases
Matrix.c1Body: Organizes disease × target × drug-candidate into a searchable matrix; every cell carries evidence — papers, trials, indications. We borrow this idea: every cell represents the existing evidence for one composite combination.
Matrix.c2Body: Structured indexing of materials by physical and process properties. MatWeb hosts 160K+ materials; Granta Enterprise is used as first reference by aerospace design firms. Our matrix is the AI-native upgrade of this tradition.
Matrix.c3Body: Three dimensions: fiber × resin × process. Columns are 11 mainstream resins (UPR / VER / Epoxy / Phenolic / PU / BMI / Cyanate / PEEK / PPS / PA / Bio-epoxy); rows are 5 fiber systems; the third axis is 8 processes. Click any cell to see every material / formula / paper / patent for that combination.
Matrix.c4Body: Traditional taxonomies let you see one dimension at a time; a matrix shows every intersection, including the ones not yet studied well. The AI uses the same matrix to recommend your next engineering move, or to tell you 'nobody has done this one'.
Matrix.matrixHint: {fibers} fibers × {resins} resins × {processes} processes = {total} combinations. Click any cell to see the full evidence subset.
Matrix.processTitle: Third dimension: eight main forming processes
Matrix.processHint: The process axis is used as a filter on the combination detail page. TP = thermoplastic matrix.
Matrix.u1Body: Click any cell in the matrix above. The detail page lists every material / formula / paper / patent we have for that combination.
Matrix.u2Body: The detail page aggregates everything in our six libraries relevant to that combination. No keyword filtering needed.
Matrix.u3Body: The AI CTA at the bottom of the detail page pre-fills a question about that combination and jumps you into the AI chat with citations.
Matrix.philosophyTitle: Treat composites as an enumerable combination space
Matrix.philosophyBody1: The core industrial-composites question is not 'how do I use this material?', but 'for my load case, which fiber × resin × process combination is best?'. That is, at heart, a search problem — find the engineering-feasible and economically optimal points in a bounded but very large combination space.
Matrix.philosophyBody2: This is exactly the path drug discovery (target × compound × indication) and chemical-space exploration (molecule × reaction × product) already walked. We borrow the same combinatorial thinking to organize composites — so both the AI and the engineer can locate, compare, and verify on the same matrix.

Combo.metaDescription: Full materials / formulas / papers / patents subset for the {name} combination.
Combo.lead: Every piece of evidence we have for the {fiber} × {resin} combination. The sections below aggregate all directly relevant materials, formulas, papers and patents in our database.
Combo.processesHint: Which process fits this combination best? Click the AI CTA for an evidence-based answer.
Combo.emptyBody: Our database has limited evidence for {name} right now — it may be a frontier or niche combination. Ask the AI for general-knowledge engineering guidance.
Combo.aiCtaTitle: Let the AI walk you through the engineering details
Combo.aiCtaBody: Ask 'under what load cases does {name} fit best? typical process parameters? recommended suppliers?' — the AI will answer based on the evidence.
Combo.aiSuggestQuery: {fiber} × {resin} combination: which load cases does it suit? Which process? Typical process parameters? Where are the matching materials and suppliers on f1frp?
Combo.verdictAnswer2: {fiber} with {resin} is a mature, mainstream industrial combination: well-established processing and a deep supply chain — safe to specify.
Combo.verdictAnswer1: {fiber} with {resin} is viable but relatively niche, used for specific load cases. Cross-check the key parameters against the evidence below and with the AI before specifying.
Combo.verdictAnswer0: {fiber} with {resin} is experimental / rare, with a limited production track record. Consider it only for special requirements, and validate with a small trial first.
Combo.verdictSource: f1frp fiber × resin feasibility matrix + live knowledge-base lookup
Combo.ctaRfqTitle: Submit an RFQ for this combination
Combo.ctaCalcTitle: Estimate mass & cost with the calculator
Combo.faqQ3: Where can I find {fiber} × {resin} materials and suppliers?
Combo.faqA2: The mainstream compatible processes are listed under 'Compatible forming processes' on this page. Which one to choose depends on part cross-section and volume — ask the on-page AI for an evidence-based recommendation.
Combo.faqA3: This page already aggregates the materials, formulas, papers and patents in the f1frp database related to this combination; click any material for detail, or reach the matching verified suppliers via RFQ / AI.

AiAgent.metaDescription: Design logic, features, implementation, usage and future of the AI Agent layer.
AiAgent.h1: AI Agent layer: citation-first, never hallucinates
AiAgent.lead: The top layer consumes the two layers below it. It is not a ChatGPT skin — it is an engineering assistant that cites whatever it finds and explicitly says 'I don't know' when it cannot.
AiAgent.d1Body: Every number, every statement, every standard code must come from the six libraries. When the model has no source, it says 'f1frp has no record of this; the following is general knowledge' — never pretends.
AiAgent.d2Body: We do not fine-tune models. Each query uses pgvector semantic search to fetch Top-K relevant records and inject them as context. New data in DB → usable same day, no retraining.
AiAgent.d3Body: Gemini 2.5 Flash handles general inference (large free tier, fast); Claude Haiku 4.5 (via OpenRouter) for higher-quality commentary. Auto-fallback on quota exhaustion or quality drop.
AiAgent.d4Body: Citation links go straight to source pages so users can verify. Future work layers 'Verified / Supplier-claimed / AI-inferred' confidence badges on top of citations.
AiAgent.f1Body: Describe the load case (stress / chemistry / temperature / budget). AI filters from 4,341 materials and returns top recommendations with citations.
AiAgent.f2Body: 102 formula records support replies. When asked 'how to formulate resin for pultrusion?' the AI cites specific formula IDs and parameters.
AiAgent.f3Body: 95 GB / ISO / ASTM / EN standards. AI gives applicable standards + chapter citations.
AiAgent.f4Body: 698+ papers and 1,473+ patents with Chinese commentary. AI cites multiple sources as evidence.
AiAgent.f5Body: Filters top-3 suppliers by material + region + certification. Paired with the RFQ button to send an inquiry directly.
AiAgent.f6Body: Locale auto-passed to AI — Chinese question gets Chinese answer, English stays English. No mixing.
AiAgent.i1Body: Every material / formula / standard / paper / patent entry has an embedding (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). embedText(query) → cosine ranking → top-8 injected into system prompt.
AiAgent.i2Body: System prompt enforces [#N] inline citations. Streaming response attaches a citations array via messageMetadata so the client can render clickable [#N] markers.
AiAgent.i3Body: @ai-sdk/google primary, @ai-sdk/anthropic + OpenRouter fallback. Per-call routing based on quota, latency, cost.
AiAgent.i4Body: Frontend uses @ai-sdk/react useChat + DefaultChatTransport. Streamed typewriter response, automatic retry on error.
AiAgent.u1Body: The search-style input under the hero. Type, press Enter → routes to the AI page and auto-sends. Best for a quick one-off question.
AiAgent.u2Body: Multi-turn conversation, scenario shortcuts, sources sidebar. Main chat on the left, Sources list on the right — each clickable to the source page.
AiAgent.u3Body: Bottom-right AI widget on every page. Mid-browse, ask about a material or formula without leaving.
AiAgent.r1Body: Upgrade from single-turn Q&A to Agent Loop. Expose materials.search / formulas.recommend / suppliers.filter as tools; AI handles multi-step tasks.
AiAgent.r2Body: pgvector namespace per paid enterprise. Upload TDS / test reports. AI cites both your private data and public libraries.
AiAgent.r3Body: One-click generation of technical report PDFs / BOM Excels / RFQ letters / spec sheets. react-pdf templates, enterprise brandable.
AiAgent.r4Body: Layer 'Verified / Supplier-claimed / AI-inferred' badges on top of citations. Unsupported claims visually marked 'uncertain'.
AiAgent.r5Body: When the AI cannot answer, one-click handoff to paid consultation with certified engineers / professors. Extends from 'AI Q&A' to 'AI + expert'.

Data.metaDescription: Design logic, features, implementation, usage and future of the structured data layer.
Data.h1: Structured data layer: a six-library knowledge graph
Data.lead: The middle layer is not a loose yellow page. Materials / formulas / standards / papers / patents / suppliers — six tables interlinked by foreign keys and semantic similarity — form a knowledge graph that always has a next step for engineers who walk in.
Data.d1Body: Material pages show related formulas / recommended suppliers / downloads; formula pages link back to material entries; paper pages show related papers; patent pages surface peer patents. Every page is an entry to the other five libraries.
Data.d2Body: Each material parameter will carry a source_type (manufacturer TDS / third-party test / AI inference). Papers link out to DOI, patents link to Google Patents.
Data.d3Body: Cron runs at 2am UTC daily, pulling from CrossRef + OpenAlex + Google Patents + RSS. Ingest → translate → Chinese commentary → sitemap refresh → multi-engine push.
Data.d4Body: Beyond the automatic cron, companies can claim their own supplier listing and fill in details; engineers can submit corrections.
Data.lib1Body: Covers resin / glass fiber (yarn / mat / fabric) / carbon / basalt / aramid / bio-based / core / gelcoat / auxiliary / composite product. Each carries mechanical, thermal, and physical properties in structured form.
Data.lib2Body: Grouped by 7 processes (hand lay-up / filament winding / pultrusion / compression molding / RTM / vacuum infusion / 3D printing). Each entry includes resin system, reinforcement, auxiliary, process parameters, expected properties, operating tips, safety notes.
Data.lib3Body: China GB / HG / JC, International ISO, American ASTM, European EN, German DIN. Organized by process and product. AI clause commentary on the roadmap.
Data.lib4Body: Aggregated from CrossRef + OpenAlex. Covers mechanics, processing, fiber reinforcement, resin matrix, durability, recycling. Each with AI Chinese commentary.
Data.lib5Body: Aggregated from Google Patents — CN / US / EP / JP / KR. Covers pultrusion / RTM / HP-RTM / thermoplastic / window/door / automotive / wind. Commentary backfill in progress.
Data.lib6Body: Real composites industry firms. Claimed companies carry contact emails that receive RFQs directly. Includes major Chinese composites leaders (Jushi, Zhongfu Shenying, Taihe, Huachang, etc.).
Data.i1Body: ap-southeast-1 region, usage-based billing. Schema: 14 tables + 5 enums. Drizzle ORM for type-safe queries.
Data.i2Body: Each entry embedded via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536-dim) and stored in knowledge_chunks with HNSW index for millisecond semantic search.
Data.i3Body: sources.ts provides unified interface to CrossRef / OpenAlex / Google Patents / RSS. Daily cron rotates through query-pool topics. Dedupes by DOI / publication number.
Data.i4Body: Gemini 2.5 Flash does translate and commentary; Claude Haiku via OpenRouter fallback on high failure. Pipeline is idempotent and re-runnable.
Data.u1Body: Every library has its own list page with multi-dimensional filters (category / brand / country / year / language / process), search, and compare.
Data.u2Body: Material pages show properties table + recommended suppliers + related formulas + downloads. Paper / patent pages show Chinese commentary + related entries + external source link.
Data.u3Body: Every [#N] in an AI answer links to a data-layer entry. Data is not isolated — it is evidence for AI answers.
Data.r1Body: Expand data itself to DE / JA / RU / ES / PT. Doubles overseas reach.
Data.r2Body: Every material parameter gets source_type (TDS / 3rd-party / AI-inferred) + confidence (0-1). UI shows Verified / Claimed / Estimated badges.
Data.r3Body: Upgrade key parameters (tensile / modulus / Tg / water-absorption) from single values to temperature × parameter series. Add S-N fatigue, creep, and water-absorption curves.
Data.r4Body: Open REST API to ERP / PLM / CAE vendors, per-call billing. Become the industry data substrate.
Data.r5Body: Grow materials from 4,341 to 100,000-scale, on par with MatWeb. Add more grades, batches, and temperature-dependent properties.

Delivery.metaDescription: Design logic, features, implementation, usage and future of the engineering delivery layer.
Delivery.h1: Engineering delivery layer: take it and ship
Delivery.lead: The bottom layer turns AI answers and data queries into artifacts engineers ship with: RFQ emails, downloads, PDF reports, online calculators, supplier contacts. Not read-only — do-ready.
Delivery.d1Body: Traditional composites sites stop at 'read the page → make your own phone call'. f1frp adds an 'engineering action' button to every page: request sample, RFQ, download, calculate, claim. Users complete something before leaving.
Delivery.d2Body: Material detail → request sample; formula detail → download PDF; standard page → AI digest; patent page → external source; supplier page → claim or RFQ. Each page does one thing well.
Delivery.d3Body: RFQ is not sent to a dead inbox — AI matches top-3 suppliers, Resend emails them, suppliers reply, and the future closes the loop with escrow and sample logistics.
Delivery.d4Body: Clerk for auth, tier-based download gating, enterprise claim flow, dashboards tailored per role (supplier vs engineer).
Delivery.f1Body: Material page 'Request Sample / Quote' button → RFQ form → POST /api/v1/rfq → AI matches top-3 verified suppliers by category → Resend email → supplier dashboard receives the lead.
Delivery.f2Body: TDS / MSDS / CAD / test reports. Tier-0 free, tier-1 registered, tier-2 Pro subscription gates.
Delivery.f3Body: /tech/calculator pultrusion selection (load → section). /tech/u-value-calculator window U-value. Browser-only, no CAE license.
Delivery.f4Body: 67 real firms claimable by owners. Upload credentials → review → receive RFQs. Free entry + Verified / Premium / Platinum paid tiers.
Delivery.f5Body: /zh/* + /en/* bilingual sitemap + hreflang. Covers Baidu / Sogou / 360 / Bing / Google / LLM search. Daily cron does six-engine push.
Delivery.f6Body: Clerk-authenticated /dashboard: overview, publish listings, inquiry messages, enterprise management, claim applications, subscription management.
Delivery.i1Body: Server Components + Route Handlers. /[locale]/* fully internationalized, /api/* server logic, /platform/* static content.
Delivery.i2Body: Path prefix /zh/ + /en/, as-needed (default zh has no prefix). messages/ split by namespace.
Delivery.i3Body: Clerk provides email / phone / OAuth login. Webhook syncs to users table. Claim flow goes from supplier_claims to enterprise association.
Delivery.i4Body: RFQ dispatch, newsletter, system notifications via Resend HTTP API. dispatchToSuppliers is non-blocking; fails soft to f1frp2015@gmail.com.
Delivery.i5Body: Pure React client components + in-house engineering formulas. Pultrusion selection references EN 13706 / GB/T 31539; U-value references GB/T 8484.
Delivery.i6Body: Production on Vercel, edge-accelerated globally. Cron declared in vercel.json. All env vars encrypted.
Delivery.u1Body: Find material → request sample → receive supplier email. Or ask the AI and jump to a recommended material, then request sample.
Delivery.u2Body: Filter supplier directory → send RFQ to multiple firms → compare replies. Every decision point has a source.
Delivery.u3Body: Claim your firm's listing → complete info → start receiving engineer-initiated RFQ emails.
Delivery.u4Body: Browse papers / patents / standards → build proposal → PDF export (on roadmap).
Delivery.r1Body: Unified warehouse + logistics + escrow account + letter of credit — turn RFQs into real transactions. Overseas buyers order Chinese samples in one click.
Delivery.r2Body: EU CBAM mandatory from 2027. Ship 'one-click CBAM report' tooling now, partnered with SGS / TÜV China for certification. Commercial terms by email.
Delivery.r3Body: Private deployment + SSO + audit logs + unlimited private libraries for design institutes / large owners / downstream OEMs (commercial terms by email).
Delivery.r4Body: Open six-library metadata via REST API, tiered billing. Let ERP / PLM / CAE vendors integrate f1frp as their data foundation.
Delivery.r5Body: Onboard certified engineers / professors for paid consulting; platform only does matching in P1 phase. Hybrid AI + human consulting model.
Delivery.r6Body: WeChat OA AI Q&A; mini-program for RFQ; Telegram channel pushes new papers / patents. Extend to user-resident channels.

Roadmap.metaDescription: From agent tool-calling to private workspace to CBAM compliance, f1frp's next-year priorities and timeline.
Roadmap.h1: What we plan to build next
Roadmap.lead: Ordered by "existing asset × highest leverage". Earlier items are more certain than later ones, but even the last one is not vaporware — every track is grounded in AI Agent / data / user-relationship assets f1frp already has.
Roadmap.r1Body: Upgrade the AI from single-turn Q&A to an Agent Loop: expose tools like materials.search / formulas.recommend / suppliers.filter / cost.estimate, let the AI decide which to call, and complete multi-step tasks ("design a wind-blade pultruded rod → select material → formula → suppliers → BOM → RFQ").
Roadmap.r1When: Q2 2026 · top priority on the AI roadmap
Roadmap.r2Body: A pgvector namespace per paid enterprise, where they upload their own TDS / MSDS / test reports. AI answers cite both the enterprise's private data and the public libraries. The strongest B2B subscription hook.
Roadmap.r2When: Q3 2026 · pairs with L1 Engineer Pro / Team
Roadmap.r3Body: Turn what consultancies hand-make — technical report PDFs, BOM Excels, RFQ letters, spec sheets — into one-click AI output. react-pdf templates with enterprise branding. The real ROI gate for paid tiers.
Roadmap.r4Body: EU CBAM mandatory from 2027. Build the "one-click CBAM report", EPD environmental declaration, and UFLPA audit tooling ahead of time, partnered with SGS / TÜV China.
Roadmap.r5Body: Overseas buyer anonymous RFQ → AI matches Chinese suppliers → sample shipping + logistics + escrow → commission 2-5% on close. Upgrades f1frp from "information" to "transactions".
Roadmap.r6Body: Open materials / formulas / standards / papers metadata as REST API to ERP / PLM / CAE vendors — making f1frp the data backbone of the industry.
Roadmap.r7Body: Onboard certified engineers / university professors / third-party labs for paid consulting. Extend the knowledge layer from databases to people.
Roadmap.r8Body: Instrument every AI answer with OpenTelemetry and user-feedback loops; build an AI citation-quality score + hallucination monitor; every AI commentary flows into a human-review channel. Trust becomes the product.

About.metaTitle: About getfrp — China FRP sourcing for overseas buyers
About.metaDescription: getfrp is an AI-native gateway to China's FRP supply chain: 200+ verified factories, GB/ASTM/EN crosswalk, and a China desk that runs the RFQ to delivery.
About.lead: China's FRP supply chain — verified, documented, exported
About.missionP1: Composites is a $100B industry running on PDF datasheets and WeChat groups. Buyers can't compare suppliers without three phone calls. Pricing is opaque. The Chinese supply base is invisible to most overseas engineers, and the few directories that exist are out of date the day they ship.
About.missionP2: We're trying to fix the part of that we can reach: a structured database of materials, formulas, standards, papers, patents, and verified Chinese suppliers, all linked, all queryable in plain English. Five fiber families covered (glass, carbon, basalt, aramid, bio). When you're ready to RFQ, a human takes over.
About.adv1Desc: 4,000+ material records with properties, processing, applications, and the suppliers who actually make them. All five fiber families.
About.adv2Desc: GB ⇄ ASTM ⇄ ISO ⇄ EN mappings for the standards that matter in FRP procurement. Tells you which Chinese standard your spec maps to before you ask the factory.
About.adv3Desc: Ask in plain English. Answers cite the underlying data with links, so you can verify before forwarding to your team.
About.adv4Desc: Our China-based sourcing desk handles the messy part: RFQ paperwork, on-site QA, payment routing, duty-exposure flags (AD/CVD, Section 301), and the conversations factory sales teams expect in Mandarin.
